published_prior_art.cite: Janson2015 supplies the finite-dependent zero-long-run-variance/coboundary classification underlying the boundary; it does not state this causal finite-projection norm.

Janson2015, Theorem 2 and Corollary 2: a finite iid block factor has zero long-run variance iff it is an L2 finite-block coboundary, with its partial sum equal to an endpoint difference and converging to the difference of independent endpoints.
ElMachkouriVolnyWu2013 gives the stationary-iid-innovation CLT substrate; the stated joint result is its standard multivariate finite-range application combined with the Janson2015 boundary law.
FanLengWu2025 estimates variance for regression-adjusted interference estimators, not a two-randomization-wave test of the zero Palm projection component.

novelty_flags.label: Theorem 2 / related_work
novelty_flags.one_line: The claimed causal coboundary equivalence, exact endpoint telescoping identity, and independent-endpoint limit are already the finite iid block-factor result of Janson2015; inserting an exposure-IPW score does not make this theorem new.

novelty_flags.label: Theorems 1–3
novelty_flags.one_line: The directly on-point Janson2015 degenerate-m-dependent-sums paper is omitted, despite subsuming the proposal's advertised zero-variance/coboundary/endpoint-law kernel.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: For a stationary finite-variance m-dependent sequence, zero asymptotic variance is equivalent to a stationary coboundary; for iid block factors the transfer is itself a finite block factor, and partial sums are endpoint differences converging to a difference of independent copies.

source_verification_receipts.version: Stochastic Processes and their Applications 123(1) (2013), pp. 1–14
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The article studies stationary fields represented as measurable transforms of iid innovations and proves CLT/invariance-principle results under a short-range dependence condition.

source_verification_receipts.version: Annales de l’Institut Henri Poincaré, Probabilités et Statistiques 51(1) (2015), pp. 89–128
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper treats Poisson stabilizing geometric functionals, establishes moderate-deviation bounds, and gives a criterion for nondegenerate limiting variance.
The paper studies treatment-effect asymptotics under a graphon-random exposure graph, gives a direct-effect CLT, and develops an indirect-effect estimator.

The paper studies randomized network experiments under approximate neighborhood interference, establishes IPW consistency and approximate normality, and analyzes network-HAC inference under a finite-population model.
The paper supplies a randomization-based exposure-mapping/IPW framework under general interference, with local-dependence consistency and asymptotic-normality results.

The preprint studies regression-adjusted interference estimators, asymptotic-variance estimation, and optimality within adjustment classes; it does not advertise a repeated-wave projection-boundary test.

source_verification_receipts.version: Theory of Probability and its Applications 6(1) (1961), pp. 87–93
source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 87–93 landing page; full theorem text paywalled
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Publication identity and its partial-sum-variance topic were verified, but the original theorem text was not accessible; Janson2015 explicitly attributes the weaker-condition coboundary representation to Leonov.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Add Janson2015 as the primary mathematical comparator and demote the coboundary/endpoint theorem to a cited corollary; make clear that any remaining contribution is a genuinely causal, observable diagnostic rather than the block-factor boundary theorem.

Replace the two-wave question with an explicit test statistic, observable inputs, and a derived minimax separation statement; establish the attainable separation scale rather than leaving an unconstrained local-power target.

To support a field contribution, extend the diagnostic beyond fixed finite-range iid block factors to a causally motivated class not covered by Janson2015, such as a rigorously specified ANI or random-stabilization regime, and prove the transfer from that published class.

recommended_next_step: Continue revision on this angle: recast Theorem 2 as known substrate, cite Janson2015, and make the two-wave observable diagnostic or a strict beyond-block-factor extension the theorem-level novelty kernel.
